caption: Government survey plat. A ring of water around an island, no name yet.
history: In 1846-47 French-Canadian families led by Jean Vadnais and Jean Garceau came up from St. Paul by ox-cart. The township was surveyed in 1848.

caption: The first map here to name it: Lamberts Lake.
history: White Bear Township was organized at John Lamb's hotel on Goose Lake on May 11, 1858, the day Minnesota became a state. 27 votes were cast.

caption: Lambert's Lake. P. Jervais on the island.
history: The Lake Superior & Mississippi Railroad is building its line from St. Paul to White Bear; trains run from 1868.
credit: L. G. Bennett, Map of Ramsey County, 1867 · UMN Libraries

caption: Lambert Lake and Lambert Island. A. K. Barnum owns the island and most of the shore.
history: White Bear is a resort town, 20 minutes from St. Paul by train. White Bear Village left the township in 1881.
credit: G. M. Hopkins, Atlas of the Environs of St. Paul, 1886, plate 19 · UMN Libraries

caption: Lambert Lake. N.W. Realty Co. owns the island.
history: Truck farms line County Road E. In the 1890s the Andersons start a 20-acre farm where Walmart stands today.
credit: P. M. Dahl, Plat Book of Ramsey County, 1898 · UMN Libraries

caption: USGS topographic map. Where the ring was, it draws marsh.
history: St. Paul bought Vadnais Lake and its shore in 1899 for $22,000, per local history; it's the city's reservoir.

caption: Lambert Creek is a ditch now: County Ditches 13 and 14.
history: In 1936 the CCC and St. Paul Water dug channels feeding East Vadnais. County Ditch 14 drains Lambert Lake in the 1940s.

caption: Air photo. The dark corner is a frame that wouldn't line up.
history: Still farms and wetlands. After the war the Vadnais area grows from about 750 people toward 2,000.
White Bear Lake keeps annexing township land; in 1956 township voters reject a 1,850-acre annexation.

caption: Air photo.
history: July 1957: the Lake Vadnais area votes 277 to 83 to become a village, over a fight about sewers. North Oaks left the township in 1956; Gem Lake follows in 1959.
credit: MHAPO, UMN Borchert Map Library (Ramsey County, 1957)

caption: Drained for development that never came. I-35E cuts through.
history: I-35E construction began in 1964 and the I-35E/I-694 'weave' opened by the early 1970s. Vadnais Heights: 3,411 people (1970).
A city since 1974, when state law made every village a city. 5,111 people (1980). In 1986 VLAWMO takes over the Lambert Creek ditches.
11,041 people (1990). Walmart anchors the city's first shopping center. Minnesota passes its Wetland Conservation Act.
City Hall opened in 2000; the farms along County Road E are gone. 13,069 people (2000), the city's peak.
'Unweave the Weave' (2004-08) splits I-35E from I-694. Lambert Lake Pond is dug in 2005 inside the old lakebed.
The Vadnais Sports Center opened in 2010. 12,302 people (2010).
Lambert Creek has been on the state's impaired-waters list for bacteria since 2008.

caption: Lambert: a wetland on Lambert Creek, flowing to East Vadnais.
history: In winter 2020-21 crews put the bends back into about 2,000 feet of straightened Lambert Creek beside the old lakebed.

caption: Today.
history: Vadnais Heights 12,912 and Gem Lake 528 people (2020). Lambert Creek still runs into St. Paul's drinking-water reservoir.
credit: Google Maps imagery, stitched from 18 screenshots
